model_annotation: Figure 3 presents two bar charts comparing inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, against two sample-level ambiguity metrics: standard deviation (left chart) and maximum ambiguity (right chart). The left chart shows three bars corresponding to Ambiguity Std bins (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), with Fleiss Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 respectively, indicating decreasing agreement as ambiguity increases. The right chart displays three bars for Max Ambiguity bins (1, 2, 3), with Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, similarly showing a decline in agreement with higher maximum ambiguity. Both charts use blue bars and include numerical Kappa values above each bar. Figure 4, a circular gradient visualization, illustrates the distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and maximum ambiguity, though specific percentages or axes are not labeled. Table 2 quantifies the number of conversations broken down by annotation status (Annotated/Unannotated) and intent (Malicious/Benign) for three modes: Single-LLM, Dual-Agent, and All, with an overall LLM Label Macro F1 score of 0.91 reported below the table.
